title: Implement fresh turns, zoom/date tools, streaming logs and steering
description:
## Background and scope
Render historical view before recording new user input; fresh API conversation each idle turn. Await complete prior leaves; append user input losslessly, then assistant replies/tool calls/tool results in observed order. During active tool work log new user inputs and inject between tool calls, or as subsequent turn if no tool boundary remains. Persist completed text blocks as streamed; never thoughts. Implement zoom(id,n,page) for aligned binary nodes, raw leaf text/images with bounded pages, and date(id). Validate arguments and return errors as tool results. Tool output sent to model and persisted must use same clipping policy. Keep within-turn signed thinking only in volatile API messages. Cancellation/provider failure retains all already committed outputs; never silently retries a tool action. Acceptance: restart continuity, no new-message duplication in initial view, corrections are delivered, tool loops terminate visibly on configured limit. Tests: scripted tool exchanges, injection ordering, cancellation, raw retrieval, invalid IDs, image reload, fresh request snapshots.

## Success criteria and test plan
Complete the acceptance and tests above, with errors carrying record/job identifiers but no secrets. Keep implementation traceable to this bead and document remaining limitations.
close_reason: Fresh turns, zoom/date/images, streaming persistence and correctly ordered tool results with live steering implemented. End-turn/failure boundaries, cancellation, oversized-input preservation and cross-process recall verified.

comments.author: gora
comments.text: Cross-model review: all tool_result blocks matching a parallel assistant tool_use batch must lead the next API user message, ahead of steering/work text. Test two tool calls plus a user interruption. Oversized user requests must be persisted fully and rejected visibly before sending an oversized API request, with continuation via bounded messages; never silently truncate.

title: Build summaries with bounded concurrent queues and contextual retries
description:
## Background and scope
Use ready queues and dependency notifications rather than scanning the historical tree on each message. Queue missing leaves on startup; leaf can start when fewer than eight earlier leaves remain unbuilt; parent starts only with both children. Up to eight async model calls. Compaction context uses only built prefix and cuts off before a leaf, or at merge end; no future messages. Same system/tools as turns, separate smaller persisted view. Task includes full source, kind and 512-dash ruler; merge has both child texts and covered IDs. Never execute compaction tool calls. Retry oversized output up to five total attempts in same conversation with actual UTF-8 size and safe cutoff; retain shortest valid line, retry failed jobs on next input or explicit compact. Commit every node exactly once. Acceptance: foreground never acts on incomplete old history; outages fail visibly without losing raw records. Tests: concurrency bound, ordering, failed jobs, contextual cutoff, Unicode oversize, malicious tool request, duplicate scheduling, startup pending work.

## Success criteria and test plan
Complete the acceptance and tests above, with errors carrying record/job identifiers but no secrets. Keep implementation traceable to this bead and document remaining limitations.
close_reason: Bounded eight-worker readiness queues, contextual summaries, five UTF-8 shortening attempts, failed-job retry and prior-leaf gating implemented. Concurrency, missing-work restart, no-tree-scan and invalid-summary tests passed.

comments.author: gora
comments.text: Cross-model review: reject empty output and any tool-using compaction. Shortest valid result means nonempty text-only result; no tool execution or truncation to fake a summary.

title: Implement binary tree addressing and deterministic batched memory views
description:
## Background and scope
Node (l,i) covers 2**l messages from i*2**l, named id+n. Preserve short sources verbatim with role tags and join short children without model work. A chronological view must cover a contiguous prefix exactly once with aligned dyadic nodes. Append only built leaves; choose adjacent sibling pairs whose parent exists by maximum (T-last_message)/2**l, ties oldest first. Above 128,000 rendered UTF-8 bytes, merge in one batch toward 64,000; if parents unavailable retain a persistent pending-batch flag and continue later. Save actual partitions, never refit at restart. Maintain an independent 16,000/32,000 compaction view and reset/coarsen it when main view batches. Render id+n lines with flattened newlines and stable four-line blocks for provider caching. Acceptance: exact coverage, stable prefixes, real byte budgets and deterministic merge order. Tests: T=10 counterexample, compare rollback push for 20,001 prefixes, unavailable parents, restart mid-batch, compaction cutoff without future-message leakage.

## Success criteria and test plan
Complete the acceptance and tests above, with errors carrying record/job identifiers but no secrets. Keep implementation traceable to this bead and document remaining limitations.
close_reason: Persisted main/compaction views, exact last-message merge order, pending batches and cutoff expansion implemented. 20,001-prefix rollback equivalence, suffix recovery and 512-message budget tests passed.

comments.author: gora
comments.text: Cross-model review: no-model child join applies only if UTF-8 bytes of left + newline + right fit the full limit, including kind tags. Persist batch intent before atomic partition updates, clear intent only after both main and compaction views are durable; restart reuses nodes and only appends missing suffix.

title: Persist append-only daily logs with exclusive ownership and indexed retrieval
description:
## Background and scope
Create main/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl records {i,kind,text,size,date} with monotonic permanent IDs and kinds user,unii,tool,echo,work,note; tree daily JSONL {l,i,text,size}; persisted view.json list of [l,i]. Lock one writer using OS process lock, flush/fsync appends, atomically replace view files with directory fsync. Index offsets rather than retain all raw text in memory. Preserve non-tool text via UTF-8-safe consecutive chunks, clip echo head/tail to 30,000 characters, persist image references and bytes for zoom. Startup must validate IDs, sizes and references and reconcile only an uncheckpointed suffix without reconstructing existing view partitions. Never silently truncate corrupt logs or rebuild missing views; provide actionable errors and explicit recovery guidance. Acceptance: restart retrieves byte-identical content, rejects competing writers/corruption, never duplicates built nodes. Tests: Unicode, daily rollover, long input, process lock, abrupt exit after append, invalid/truncated records, snapshots and attachment integrity.

## Success criteria and test plan
Complete the acceptance and tests above, with errors carrying record/job identifiers but no secrets. Keep implementation traceable to this bead and document remaining limitations.
close_reason: Append-only fsynced logs, exclusive lock, indexed retrieval, image integrity, fail-stop writes and idempotent event chunks implemented. Storage fault/restart/Unicode tests passed.

title: Add streaming Anthropic transport with stable prompt caching and offline demo
description:
## Background and scope
Implement async provider interface and standard-library HTTPS/SSE Anthropic Messages transport. Read API key from environment only; configurable turn and compaction model IDs, bounded timeout and token output. Same stable system and tool definitions for turns and compactions; use four-line view blocks, cache last whole block and request end with five-minute ephemeral cache marks plus stable-system mark. Serialize concurrent writes of identical model/account/prefix only until message_start, releasing waiters on errors/cancellation. Decode text, thinking, signed blocks, tool-use partial JSON and usage events; thoughts remain ephemeral and never enter logs. Surface HTTP, stream and truncation errors without pretending completion; no paid calls in deterministic tests. Demo is explicitly fake. Acceptance: real provider request shape conforms to official API, streaming text and tools work, cache metrics are available. Tests: local fake HTTP server/SSE, errors, malformed/truncated stream, cache coordination, differing models, secret-free errors.

## Success criteria and test plan
Complete the acceptance and tests above, with errors carrying record/job identifiers but no secrets. Keep implementation traceable to this bead and document remaining limitations.
close_reason: Anthropic SSE transport, tool JSON, volatile thinking, usage, cache marks and response-start coordination implemented. Mock/local HTTP tests and subprocess cancellation test passed; no real API claims.

comments.author: gora
comments.text: Cross-model review: cache sharing is scoped to model/account. Default distinct main and summary models do not share cache entries; identical stable tools/system only permit sharing when model/account also match. No transparent retry after ambiguous stream failures.

title: Support explicitly requested asynchronous subagents with separate transcripts
description:
## Background and scope
Optional user-invoked /agent NAME TASK starts a fresh call with current main view plus task. Own replies/tool steps remain under agents/NAME with separate durable transcript, not in main log. Exactly one final work message [Name] report enters master through same steering path or starts a new turn. Expose zoom(Name) pagination of isolated chat. Do not expose autonomous spawning to model; user explicitly invokes. Prevent duplicate names/path traversal; recover unfinished jobs as interrupted rather than rerun external actions. Main turn must never wait or poll for agents; CLI may let user explicitly wait for tasks at shutdown. Acceptance: live reports arrive without user polling and parent remains responsive. Tests: isolation, final report delivery, invalid names, task failure, restart visibility and named zoom.

## Success criteria and test plan
Complete the acceptance and tests above, with errors carrying record/job identifiers but no secrets. Keep implementation traceable to this bead and document remaining limitations.
close_reason: Explicit asynchronous named agents, separate transcripts and durable report outbox implemented. Isolation, names, complete-report recovery and interrupted chunk delivery tests passed.

title: Ship a usable terminal interface and offline end-to-end demonstration
description:
## Background and scope
Provide python -m eternalchat and installed eternalchat entrypoint. Commands chat, ask, note/import, view, zoom, date, compact and status; --data-dir, --demo, model and instruction configuration. Interactive reader remains responsive during active requests, supports /agent, /attach, /status, /zoom, /quit, displays text and optional ephemeral thinking, and clear errors. EOF drains submitted user inputs; shutdown finishes/cancels tasks explicitly without corrupting store. Document API key setup, example session, recovery, model-specific cache limits and optional absent device tools. Acceptance: fresh checkout runs offline with no dependencies and real API path configurable. Tests: subprocess two-run persistence, input piping, no-key failure, live steering, import and compact, machine-readable status and diagnostic progress.

## Success criteria and test plan
Complete the acceptance and tests above, with errors carrying record/job identifiers but no secrets. Keep implementation traceable to this bead and document remaining limitations.
close_reason: Interactive and one-shot terminal commands, imports, attachments, inspection, demo mode, API configuration and recovery instructions shipped. Installed command and subprocess CLI smoke passed.

title: Define the executable UniiChat contracts and package layout
description:
## Background and scope
Implement EternalChat as a Python 3.11+ local terminal application with an importable asynchronous core and no runtime dependencies. Source: VictorTaelin gist 91837951a5ce5b38f341ec1ba1df6449, revision 3c190e06f34aba0c69f49042c526093269604935 (2026-10-08). The single chat is its memory; fresh turns receive only a persisted summary view plus the new message. Freeze stable instructions and tools per process. Define defaults: 512 UTF-8 bytes per summary; main view 64,000/128,000 bytes; compaction view 16,000/32,000; eight compactions; five shortening attempts. Resolve contradictory placeholders by admitting only completed summaries and gating turns on all prior leaves. Preserve shortest nonempty summary after five attempts even if over target. Explicitly document character-based tool clipping, image assets, crash behavior, provider configuration, and optional subagents/device scope. Acceptance: installable module/CLI, documented data and recovery contracts, validated configuration. Tests: invalid budgets, multibyte splitting, source-derived boundary cases, runnable offline commands.

## Success criteria and test plan
Complete the acceptance and tests above, with errors carrying record/job identifiers but no secrets. Keep implementation traceable to this bead and document remaining limitations.
close_reason: Python package, validated configuration, CLI entry point, README and source contract map implemented. Editable install and installed-command demo passed.
